maria: ran an end-to-end perf pass on canary after the kernel selector tweak, noticed a weird regression on small-chat workloads.
aj: what numbers are you seeing? :thinking_face:
maria: p50 went from ~42ms -> 58ms, p95 from 120ms -> 185ms, throughput down ~18% for batch sizes <= 4. Full log: `bench/2026-03-17/small-chat-run.log` (short snippet below).
aj: ouch. did the KV priming change land in that branch too? could be cold KV misses.
maria: no KV code in that PR, only kernel selection heuristics + the new token-budget allocator. but I did see increased KV cache load stalls in the timeline.
sasha: can you paste the profiler flame? curious if CPU stalls or GPU enqueue gaps.
maria: pasted a small profile excerpt:
```
TIMELINE: |---prefill---|---decode---|
GPU enqueue gaps: multiple 800us holes during prefill->decode handshake
KV cache hit ratio: 0.78 -> 0.62 (samples during canary)
kernel switch counts per request: 3 -> 5
```
chen: kernel switch counts up to 5 is suspicious. that increases host->device round trips for tiny requests.
aj: maybe the new kernel affinity policy overprefers a high-throughput kernel that is bad for short sequences.
sasha: suggested experiment: keep kernel affinity, but separate prefill/decode queue policies so small prefill batches don't get funneled to the same kernel as long decodes.
maria: tried a patch that separates queues by phase and assigns token budgets: prefill budget 8 tokens, decode budget 128 tokens, and a small-batch preference for kernels with <2ms launch overhead.
ops-bot: deploy canary 4767890123-pha-sep to 1/10 hosts (status: success)
maria: after that canary: p50 down to 45ms, p95 130ms, throughput back to -2% vs baseline. KV hit ratio improved to 0.74.
aj: good sign. can you share the queue config you used?
maria: config snippet:
```
queue_policies:
  - name: prefill-small
    phase: prefill
    token_budget: 8
    kernel_pref: fast-launch
  - name: decode-default
    phase: decode
    token_budget: 128
    kernel_pref: high-throughput
handshake_timeout_us: 1200
kv_warmup_policy: incremental-priming(0.1)
```
sasha: incremental-priming(0.1) meaning 10% of requests do a KV-priming pass? is that sampled or deterministic?
maria: sampled. we prime on the first decode for sampled requests to warm KV without priming every request.
chen: two potential follow-ups:
- tighten handshake timeout to 600us for hosts with low enqueue jitter
- add a kernel-launch cost estimate to the scheduler so tiny batches avoid high-launch kernels
aj: +1. also we should add a regression test that runs a small-chat workload on every kernel-selector change and asserts p95 within 1.25x.
maria: logged issues:
- infra#3124 add small-chat perf gating job
- runtime#417 token-budget per-phase flag
- runtime#418 kernel-launch-cost metric
sasha: can we also collect per-request kernel-switch histogram in production (sampled 0.5%)? would help root cause.
maria: adding that to the follow-up list.
aj: for rollout plan: revert selector tweak in prod if canary doesn't meet p95 SLA by monday, else ship phase-aware queueing behind feature flag and ramp.
maria: creating a PR with tests + config toggles, will ping for review. thanks all :thumbsup!
